analysis.title: Now You Can See Everything: on the midterms, AI, markets, the Theranos film and corporate fraud
key_insights: The 2026 midterms were a Democratic rout. The NYT projected 53 Democratic Senators plus 2 Independents who caucus with them, and 257 Democratic House members, as of 3 am. This is the sixth midterm since 1910 in which the President's party held both chambers and lost them.

Cembalest says midterms are rarely market-moving. The business cycle drives markets, through 10-year yields, commodity prices, Fed policy, corporate profits, budget deficits, defense spending, the pace of AI investment over the next 12 months, and AI companies' borrowing needs and their effect on credit spreads.

Local ballot measures opposing data centers won or are winning almost everywhere, with North Dakota the only exception. The report is watching for governor-imposed constraints on new data center builds.

Data center capacity expected in 2027 is 37 GW, 75% of it under construction, so it is not at risk. The 96 GW expected in 2028 is more exposed. Based on election results, 37.5 GW may face a pause and another 15 GW may face conditions.

Conditions on data centers could include requiring them to pay grid costs, ending tax incentives, water limits, onsite backup power requirements, labor requirements and bans on non-disclosure agreements during permitting. Cembalest says most of these seem sensible to him.

If the data center buildout slows, upgrading to better NVIDIA chips might be the only way to generate more tokens. Google's head of data center energy said data centers in space would cost 100x more than on earth.

The recent AI market selloff appears influenced by hedge fund profit-taking. Gross long-short hedge fund exposure has fallen 8% from its recent peak, the largest drawdown since 2016 (Morgan Stanley Prime Brokerage, October 30, 2026).

Only 15% of debt and lease commitments appear on balance sheet for the big seven AI companies, and about $4 trillion of AI obligations are off balance sheet. Their credit default swap spreads have been widening rapidly.

PEG ratios (P/E divided by projected 2-5 year EPS growth) have fallen for the big seven AI firms relative to other sectors and markets, which the report reads as market suspicion of the AI earnings boom.

Cembalest lists the factors he thinks drove voters: prices (Iran War commodity spike and tariffs on core inflation), corruption, housing, labor, healthcare costs, rising interest rates, weak consumer spending, defense munitions depletion and rule of law.
Commodity prices are up sharply since the Iran War began on Feb 27, 2026. Retail diesel and shipping fuel are up 67%, jet fuel 65%, WTI 44% and retail gasoline 40%.
The federal budget deficit is high and worsening during an expansion for the first time since 1970. Rising Fed policy rates and long-term rates are attributed mostly to the deficit.
Cembalest expects little post-election litigation given the margins. In the 2020 cycle, GOP plaintiffs filed 79 lawsuits and won 6, none involving fraud allegations.

The report spends several pages on the Theranos film, Elizabeth Holmes, David Boies and Tim Draper. It argues that fraud damages investor confidence, multiples and market stability, and that those who conceal or intimidate whistleblowers are as culpable as those who commit fraud.
Brookings estimated that corporate fraud accounted for 10% to 24% of lost stock market wealth in the 2001-2002 decline, with a base case of 17%.

A study of Arthur Andersen clients suggests auditors uncover only about one third of actual fraud, putting the true fraud rate at 7%-10% of large public companies per year. A June 2026 NBER paper found 1.85% of VC-backed firms raising over $10 mm were involved in detected fraud from 2000 to 2023.

The Trump DoJ terminated pending investigations in non-immigration categories at a record pace. White-collar cases referred but declined in the first six months of 2025 were 6,009, versus an average of 3,787 for the prior three administrations (+59%).

sector_views.rationale: Selloff tied to hedge fund profit-taking and off balance sheet liabilities. Data center buildout faces state-level pause and conditions risk, mainly for 2028 capacity.

macro_indicators.indicator: Hedge fund gross long-short exposure drawdown
macro_indicators.interpretation: Largest drawdown since 2016, consistent with profit-taking behind the AI selloff.

macro_indicators.indicator: WTI crude price change since start of Iran War
macro_indicators.interpretation: Part of the commodity price shock that the report says weighed on voters and core inflation.

macro_indicators.indicator: Retail diesel price change since start of Iran War
macro_indicators.interpretation: Largest move in the commodity list the report shows.

macro_indicators.reading: 96 GW, of which 37.5 GW may be paused and 15 GW conditioned
macro_indicators.interpretation: The 2028 pipeline is where election outcomes could slow the buildout.

crypto_views: The Trump family enrichment tracker (The New Yorker) includes crypto gains such as World Liberty Financial stakes, token sales, stablecoin income and a stake in American Bitcoin. It put the total at $4 billion by January 2026, net of a downward adjustment for lower Bitcoin prices.
risk_factors: State-level pauses or conditions on data center construction, mainly affecting 2028 capacity.
About $4 trillion of off balance sheet AI obligations and widening credit spreads for AI companies.
Heavy borrowing needs of AI companies feeding into credit spreads.
Budget deficit rising during an expansion, pushing up long-term rates.
Tariffs and Iran War energy costs on core inflation.
Weak consumer confidence, with half of consumer spending coming from the top income decile.
Rule of law concerns: record termination of DoJ cases including white-collar crime.

vol_and_positioning: Equity long/short hedge fund gross exposure is down 8% from its running peak, the largest drawdown since 2016 (Morgan Stanley Prime Brokerage, October 30, 2026).
Five-year CDS spreads for select AI stocks (Oracle, SpaceX, Broadcom, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft) have widened rapidly, per the report.
geopolitical: Iran War: US commodity prices rose sharply from Feb 27, 2026 and the war added to core inflation alongside tariffs.
The US used more Tomahawk missiles in the first month of the Iran War than in any prior conflict, and replenishment will take years.
2026 midterms: Republicans lost both chambers according to NYT projections.
